card: Optimizes FastGEMul in the Python test framework's secp256k1 implementation by accumulating windowed additions in Jacobian coordinates instead of affine coordinates, reducing modular inversions to one per multiplication. This addresses slow execution times in secp256k1-heavy tests, with the author measuring a ~4x speedup for fixed-base multiplication and ~38% speedup for feature_taproot.py. Unit tests cross-checking results against generic GE.mul are included.
evidence: Author reports in the PR description and commit message: 'Speeds up fixed-base multiplication ~4x and feature_taproot.py ~38% (M1 Pro).'
problem: Fixed-base point multiplication in the Python secp256k1 test library performs affine point additions with repeated modular inversions across windows, causing secp256k1-intensive functional tests to execute slowly.

risk.why: A math bug in the test-only secp256k1 implementation could cause false test failures or hide regressions in functional tests.

summary: Optimizes `FastGEMul` in the functional test framework's secp256k1 Python implementation by accumulating windowed table entries in integer Jacobian coordinates. This defers modular inversion to a single operation at the end of the scalar multiplication rather than inverting on every window addition. It also adds unit tests checking `FastGEMul` against generic `GE.mul` and testing Jacobian edge cases.
